note: Which of this engine's public core exports anything outside core actually calls, and which ones are recorded as isolated. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-358 retired six families of unconsumed core surface by hand, one module at a time, because nothing measured the gap: the barrel could grow a symbol nobody outside core ever called and every gate stayed green. platform-doctor's unusedExports leg reads this file and turns red on a symbol with no consumer that is not recorded below, and on a recorded entry that has since gained a consumer or whose symbol no longer exists. The second half is what keeps this file a register rather than an amnesty: the leg makes an entry leave the moment its debt is paid. It does not refuse a new entry -- recording an isolated symbol here is one of the three ways its own remedy names to go green -- so this list shrinking is a review obligation, not a machine one.
consumerRootsRationale: The three surfaces the charter names as consumers of core: the CLI, the host hooks, and the portal. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-363 names one more file, scripts/backfill-work-summaries.mjs: it is the one-shot chain-write tool that gives the records predating the summary field one, and it derives each summary by calling core's deriveWorkSummary rather than by carrying a second copy of the rule. It is listed as a single file, not as scripts/, so the widening admits exactly the one consumer it was opened for. Test files under these roots are excluded by the leg itself rather than by this list -- a symbol whose only caller is its own test is the shape STORY-358 spent an Epic removing, and admitting tests would have reported every one of those modules as consumed on the day before it was deleted. Widening this list is the way to make a red result green without connecting anything, which is exactly why it is written down here instead of being compiled into the leg; no verb checks who widened it, so a widening is judged in review. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-364 names one more file on the same terms, scripts/knowledge-language.mjs: it is the one-shot migration executor that gives the cards written before the artefact-language policy existed their translated fields and their phrasings, and it decides both by calling core's detectLanguage and applyWriteLanguagePolicy through the barrel rather than by carrying a second copy of the rule. It is listed as a single file, not as scripts/, so the widening admits exactly the one consumer it was opened for. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-372 names scripts/dispatch-telemetry-hook.mjs: it is the host hook that calls the telemetry append/create surface through the barrel, while the telemetry reader stays consumed by packages/cli/src. Each file is listed singly so the consumer set does not widen to all scripts/. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-467 R3 retires scripts/dispatch-telemetry-hook.mjs, so it leaves the roots with the hook. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-467 R3 retires the output-contract injection hook script and the stop pact tool tree, so they leave the roots with the hooks.
regeneration: Empty allowedUnconsumed, run node scripts/platform-doctor.mjs --platform-root <container>, and the red result's unconsumedWithoutAllowance is the measured set. There is no generator script: a second implementation of this measurement is a second answer waiting to disagree with the leg's.
allowedUnconsumedRationale: The measured isolation debt at 8728bf5, recorded rather than retired. Every entry is a public export of packages/core/src/index.ts that the CLI, the hooks and the portal do not call. Recording it is not approval: it is the first time the number has been visible at all. The leg forces an entry out the moment its symbol is retired or gains a consumer; it does not refuse a new one, so keeping this list moving down is a review obligation rather than a machine one. Retiring these is the work the charter's isolation rule schedules, not work this Story does -- STORY-358 showed each family costs its own barrel edit, its own registry updates and its own gate round, and doing 484 of them in the Story that installs the meter would have buried the meter. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-380 removed one entry, validateSettingValue: packages/cli/src/index.ts's settings-set branch now calls it directly, so it has a consumer and the leg would report it as a stale allowance. The list moves down by one for the reason it was built to move -- a symbol gained a caller -- not by an act of pruning. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-366 added two entries, KnowledgeArticleCreateInput and KnowledgeArticleRefreshInput: the article verbs' input types are exported beside createKnowledgeArticle and refreshKnowledgeArticle for the same reason CreateKnowledgeUnitInput and CaptureKnowledgeUnitInput already sit in this list -- the CLI passes object literals and never names the type, so the symbol has no consumer in a recorded root. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-370 removes the persona renderer exports and retains the profile/library and historical workspace functions as explicitly non-live compatibility surfaces; they are covered by direct compatibility tests and are not public CLI routes. TCRN-CROSS-EPIC-141 (STORY-466 and STORY-467) adds three modules whose public symbols the recorded roots do not name: packages/core/src/names.ts (the name constants and the legacy alias table, read by scripts through scripts/lib/names.mjs and by tests), packages/core/src/legacy-workspace.ts (the read-only old-layout reader behind chain-validate, whose helpers and types the CLI reaches only through validateLegacyChain and openLegacyWorkspace) and packages/core/src/file-lock.ts (the engine write lock the CLI takes through withWorkspaceWriteLock). They are recorded here rather than left red; withWorkspaceLease and WorkspaceLease leave the list with the lease they belonged to. The authority removal (STORY-467 R2) leaves listGatesByWorkItem and the GateRecord type without a consumer in the recorded roots once gate-list went: gate records still replay, and the pure reader stays for them. STORY-467 R3 retires the dispatch-* verbs, so readDispatchConfig and resolveDispatch lose their CLI consumer; scripts/host-render.mjs, outside the recorded roots, still reads them until the host wiring is redecided (STORY-477). The hook scripts STORY-467 R3 retires were the last consumers of activeBinding in the recorded roots. STORY-467 R2 reduces release trust to the install-tree digest in packages/core/src/install-tree-digest.ts; its readers are scripts/lib/release-trust.mjs (the einzbern-release-verify entry), outside the recorded roots, and the engine-update verb STORY-471 adds to the CLI. STORY-469 R3 and R5 add packages/core/src/device-home.ts (the device directory, EINZBERN_HOME, and the paths of the device file, registry, cache, locks, backups and engine versions) and packages/core/src/atomic-file.ts (temporary file, flush and rename with retries on EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY); the library, stream and registry modules that follow in EPIC-141 read them inside core, and machine settings reach the CLI through machineSettingsPath. STORY-468 R1 adds packages/core/src/device-identity.ts (device.json in the device directory: the device id, its display name and their validation); the library stream writer that EPIC-141 adds next reads it inside core. STORY-469 R1 adds packages/core/src/ether-library.ts (a library's root: the manifest, README and .gitignore, created and opened); the engine switch in EPIC-141 reads it inside core. STORY-468 R2 and R3 add packages/core/src/akasha.ts (each device's stream in a library: segments, the stream manifest, the device-local write lock, clock assignment, reading one stream); the engine switch in EPIC-141 reads it inside core, and deriveLegacyEventId moves to the protocol package so an imported stream and the old-layout reader share it. STORY-468 R3 to R5 and STORY-470 R4 add the merged read of a library (readAllStreams with a timeout per file, materializeLibrary with its version vector, rejected events and key aliases); the CLI takes them up when the engine switches to libraries. STORY-469 switches the engine to libraries: initializeLibrary takes the place of the old layout's creation (its options type is exported with it), WORKSPACE_STORAGE_VERSION and ExplicitRoot stay as the old layout's read-side shapes, and the storage backends, storage-home sentinel, storage migration, replay-snapshot and view writers of the old layout leave the list with the code; the CLI now reaches the library opener, the merged read and the alias lookup directly.
